groups.title: the local readfirst command: argument parsing, git file listing, init/prompt/check/read/diff and the agent brief

checks.why: init, check, prompt, read and diff end to end on a scratch git repository

risks.text: repoFiles lists untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude, so a stray scratch file in the working tree makes `check` fail and shows up in `diff`

parse() knows its options from two lists, `FLAGS` (on/off) and `VALUES` (take a value, also as --name=value); any other --option is an error, so a new option must go into one of them or every use of it fails with 'unknown option'. Before 0.26.4 an unknown option took the next word as its value (hook --new-flag --stop ran the wrong hook). A `hook` call (not --install) never fails on its own arguments or errors: main() answers with a systemMessage warning and exit 0, because exit 2 from a PreToolUse hook refuses the tool call (an older readfirst that did not know --gate stopped every Edit and Bash call of a session, 2026-11-08)

`check` reports map problems and exits 1. prompt goes through loadMap, which settles the map as check does (settleMap) and throws (exit 2 from bin) only on what check fails on. read, diff, view, verify and export --cursor use loadMapLenient (read and diff, and the PreToolUse hook and audit, also work with no map at all: they then show only where the code broke before, from git history, and `readList` gets a null map): they only note on stderr when the map is behind the code (files in no group, patterns for deleted files) and still throw when the map is broken in itself (mapProblems with placement: false) - src/cli.mjs:173
the pattern syntax in the agent brief (`agentBrief`, src/prompt.mjs) must match what src/map.mjs accepts (`matcher`); if you change the pattern rules, update the brief as well

runHook swallows every error and returns null (exit 0, no output), so a bug in it looks the same as 'nothing to say' and the edit goes ahead; only a test with real map data would catch it. Since 2026-11-13 the catch keeps what failed as `failed:<tool>:<error>` in the hook state, which the Stop hook's line and `hook --report` name; and a shell reader (shellWrites, bashReads, passed in as `readers` so a test can give one that throws) that throws no longer reaches it: the whole command becomes a write readfirst cannot place (`misread:` with `commandKey`'s hash, refused once with --gate like any `unknown:` write, let through when made again). Until then a reader that threw (a stack overflow on deep nesting) let the command through with no word. It also uses repoFiles, readMapFile and mapProblems, so changes there change the hook. A map broken in itself (a rule naming a renamed file, bad JSON) does not silence it: both hooks open with brokenMapLine and still give what the map gives (the Stop hook blocks once with it); before 0.26.4 they said nothing for the whole repository

verify runs the map's check commands with the shell in the repository root; a map is repository content and its commands run with the user's rights, so verify stays an explicit command, never called from the PreToolUse hook or the Action. The one exception is the opt-in Stop hook (`hook --install --verify`), and it runs only commands the base branch's map already lists (trustedRuns): a command a branch adds or changes is named, never run, so checking out someone's branch cannot run their new command. On the base branch itself (main with no origin/main) trustedRuns reads the map at the last commit older than the session's first mark, never HEAD: in 0.26.4 a command the session committed to the map ran. Every file readfirst writes in the checkout (init, fix, export --cursor, verify --record, view's default page) goes through mustBeInside first, and setup through outsideRepo: a symlink that leads outside the repository stops the write. A check the Stop hook does not run blocks the stop once per state of the files (a `notrun:` mark in the hook state) and tells the agent to run `npx readfirst verify`; before 0.27.1 it passed with a note.

the MCP server (`mcpHandler`, `serveMcp`) answers by calling main() again with --root for each tool call, so anything a command prints to stdout becomes the tool's text; stdout is also the JSON-RPC channel, so `mcp` itself must never write anything else to stdout. `mcp` is handled before main() looks up the repository (so it starts outside a git repository): it must not use root, files or the map itself, and the repository is looked up at each tool call (--root, or git rev-parse in the current directory), where a failure comes back as an isError result 'not inside a git repository'

brokeBefore (src/history.mjs) runs one `git log` per code file for read, diff, the hook and the Action, and never throws: a missing git, a non-repository or a repository with no commits gives {} (nothing shown). A shallow clone with fewer than 200 commits gives { notFetched: true } for files with nothing to show, so a test that runs read in a `--depth 1` clone sees 'history not fetched'; a clone fetched to depth 200 or more counts as having the history

runHook and runStopHook find the repository from each edited file, not from the session's folder: a session can start in a folder above several repositories, and the hook state keeps absolute paths (older state files with relative paths still read against the session's repository). The state is append-only (readfirst-hook-<session>.lines in the temp folder, one [key, time] JSON line per marked file, written in one append): hooks of one session run at the same time, and reading and rewriting one JSON object lost the files of all but the last writer. The older .json object file is still read (readSeen) and never written. Each path is resolved through symlinks first (physical(): the nearest existing folder through realpath), because git gives the physical top level: a file reached through a linked folder (/tmp/lnk -> /tmp/x/r, or macOS /var -> /private/var) would otherwise be outside its repository and the hook silent. Looking the root up from event.cwd again would make the hook silent in that setup (rootOf finds it per file) - src/cli.mjs:530

the PreToolUse hook reads Bash commands too: src/bash-writes.mjs names the files a command writes (redirects, sed -i / perl -i, tee, cp/mv destinations, git checkout of paths, code that writes run by python/node/sh from -c, -e or a here-document: only the targets of its write calls, resolved by codeTargets from a literal, an assigned variable, a parameter, a for-loop, a glob or the script's arguments, falling back to the files it names that exist) and only those; file arguments are read per command through OPTIONS/options() in bash-writes.mjs: < and 2> redirects and option values (truncate -s N, sed -e/-f SCRIPT, cp/mv/install -t DIR, which is then the destination) are dropped first, and only -i, -i<suffix>, --in-place or a flag cluster reaching i make sed/perl write (perl -M<module>, -I<dir> do not); a command whose options are not in `OPTIONS` gets no option values dropped; segments split at ; && | |& a single & (background; not the & of &&, >&, &>, <& or an escaped \&: until 2026-11-13 `cmd & sed -i x f` hid the sed) and newlines outside quotes only, so node -e "a; fs.writeFileSync(f)" stays one command, and a here-document belongs to the last command on its line and its paths start after the cds before it; variables and writes it cannot place: the risk on shellWrites; a command that merely reads or runs tests must give none, or every Bash call would carry notes. The matcher in installHook and plugins/readfirst/hooks/hooks.json includes Bash; with --gate the first call on an unseen file is denied with the notes and the retry passes, because the notes mark the file as seen. Quotes are read from the bracket table (the risk on scanText): they open again inside $( ) (so a > in python3 -c "..." inside "$(...)" is code, not a redirect; a regex once read `i>=0` there as a write to `=0`), and a quote that never closes is a plain character; $(( )) and $[ ] are blanked as quotes are

`shellWrites` (src/bash-writes.mjs, since 2026-11-13) gives a Bash command's writes as { files, unknown, repos }; bashWrites is its files. Words are read as the shell reads them (`shellWord`: quotes, backslash escapes, $NAME and ${NAME}), with the variables the command sets for itself (`follow`: NAME=value alone, in order; export, declare, local, readonly; a ( ) keeps its own; NAME=value before a command is that command's alone; cd sets PWD and OLDPWD) and those it starts with (`vars`: the hook passes its own environment, so $TMPDIR and $HOME are known; one not set there is not). What cannot be known (a variable set nowhere, a $( ), ${NAME:-x}, $1, a loop or read variable, relative paths after cd $D) is never named and never dropped: `unknown` gives the part, why and `prefix` (the folder it is known to be under). `$(mktemp ...)` is a new name in a known folder (`mktempUnder`: -p, --tmpdir, -t, the template's folder; `fresh`), a part only inside a file's name (`out-$k.txt`) is `direct` (nothing below), and a part inside one folder name (`/tmp/zz-$r/f`) is `within` (dir, pre, post): only folders of that shape below dir, not all of it. repos: the checkouts the command makes (git worktree add, clone, init); a write into one whose folder is known in full is listed in that checkout, not there yet. The PreToolUse hook (`couldLandIn` in src/cli.mjs, whatever folder the session runs in) refuses once with --gate (`unknown:<hash>`) when the write could land in a repository: the one holding its prefix, or (not fresh, not direct) one below it that the session used, that the command makes or that `reposUnder` finds on disk (`within` narrows the walk; 2000 folders and a fifth of the budget shared across the walks, a cut walk counts as possible); no prefix: any. The refusal names five and counts the rest. Otherwise it is outside them all and quiet. The second review of 2026-11-13 found `/tmp/zz-$r/f` walked all of /tmp (12 s) and named hundreds of repositories

`follow` (src/bash-writes.mjs) believes a value only where the command surely sets it; a wrong value is worse than none, because it names a file with confidence. A $( ) or backticks holding | ; or && (`S=$(echo b | tr b c)`) is one word, taken out of the command (lift), and makes an assignment of a value not known; its operators are not the command's. A pipeline's stage sets nothing after it; `+=` appends; printf -v, mapfile, readarray, getopts, let and (( )) make the names they set not known; export keeps its mark when the value is set later or again, and export -n takes it off. An assignment word has no command name (`E=/s/eval` once read as eval). `git -C /abs` runs in /abs (it was joined under the command's folder). A value holds inside the block that sets it (`howItRuns` keeps `state.blocks`: what was there before each if/loop, so else/elif start again from before the if and what the block changed is not known after it) and after a command of an && / || list only until the list ends (`eachCommand` keeps `state.chain`); in a loop a relative cd and a value built from itself (`S=$S/x`) grow each turn and are not known (`turning`); a `for` over a literal list gives its variable those values (`values`, expanded by `perTurn`), so a write through it is a write to each. A case arm is read after its `pattern)` (`caseHead` splits heads, also after `{`, `if`, a wrapper or a pattern) and starts from before the case (`branchAgain`; after `;&` from either); a block after `do` or a wrapper is a block. Functions, subshells, source and eval: the risk after this one. Each walk of the segments (shellWrites, stateAt, bashReads, commandWords) goes through `eachCommand`, which reads the text without here-document bodies (`hereDocs`, as bash finds them) and with substitutions taken out (lift): a new walk written beside it loses these rules.

`follow` (src/bash-writes.mjs) for functions and subshells. A function's { } body runs when it is called, not where it is written: a definition is `f()`, `f ()`, `f ( )`, `f(){` or `function f` (`definition`; `f ( )` was read as a call of f until 2026-11-13), and its { may stand on the next line (`fnAwait`, which a blank or comment line leaves waiting). How deep the body is, is counted in one place, `howItRuns`, on the words before opening() takes a leading { off them (`braces`): { and } count only where a command could start (first, after `(`, `do`, `then`, `!`, `time`, a `()`, a closing `)`, or `fi`/`done`/`esac`). Until 2026-11-13 any word ending in { or starting with } counted: `echo {` in a body made it one deeper, so the { cd /b; } group after the function was taken for its body and its cd was lost; `echo }` ended it; and a { } group inside the body, its { already taken off, ended the body early. The body's first command on the definition's line is read as any line of it is (`f() { if cd /a` runs cd); a ( ) body is a subshell and never moves the caller. A call of a function the command defines makes every variable not known, and the folder too when the function may cd (`mayCd`: cd, pushd, popd, source, `.`, eval, exec, builtin, command, a command named by a variable, a function that may, or a name defined twice); eval, source and `.` do both. `command`/`builtin`/`time cd` move this shell. A ( after `time`, `!`, `do`, `then`, `else`, or `if`/`elif`/`while`/`until` (`if (cd /a; ...); then`), also after such a word inside another ( (`time (time (cd /a; ...))`: until 2026-11-13 the inner cd was not followed), opens a subshell (`parens`): its cd ends at its ), and (( )) there is arithmetic, not two subshells. follow takes time/command/builtin and the ( or { after them off as many times as they come.

A (( that is two subshells (`((cd d; echo > h) )`: bash reads (( as arithmetic only when the ) of its inner ( is followed at once by another )) is decided by the bracket table on the whole text, and eachCommand writes it `( (` before splitting it (`spaced`): split at its ;, `((cd d` alone looks like arithmetic that never closes, and opening() keeps a word starting with (( as the arithmetic command, so the write and the cd were lost until 2026-11-14. opening() and howItRuns drop a word that is only ( or { and read the next word the same way: `( (cd d; ...) )` and `{ (cd d; ...); }` left `(cd` as the command name, and the cd was not followed.

A here-document's body is data, never commands of this shell (hereDocs takes it out), with one exception (2026-11-14): when its tag is not quoted (`<<E`, not `<<'E'`, `<<"E"` or `<<\E`), bash expands the body before the command gets it, so each $( ) and backtick in it runs. shellWrites reads those (`docSubstitutions`, from the bracket table read with `doc`: in a body, as inside "...", a quote is a plain character) as commands where the command stands, after the cds before it; a shell fed the body reads them with its commands instead. They were not read at all: `cat <<E` with `$(echo > f)` in its body made f and nothing was named. bashReads and commandWords still leave bodies out. withoutComments starts a comment only where a word starts, read in the text itself: after a blank not escaped by a backslash, the line start, or ; & | < > (not a ), which may close a $( ) the word goes on after). In the blanked text a quote just closed is a space, so `'[1]'#x` lost `#x` and `echo 'a'#b > f` its redirect, and `echo a\ #b > f` lost its write too, until 2026-11-14. A backslash and a newline are taken out in one place, hereDocs, in the same walk, where bash takes them out (code, "...", $( ), backticks, a body under a tag not quoted), not in '...', a comment or a body under a quoted tag, and not after an escaped backslash or before a CR: `a\` + newline + `#b` is the word a#b, and `# note \` ends at its line. Before, each reader joined them first over the whole text. test/here-docs.test.mjs runs both against bash. A here-document is read where bash expands it, before its command runs, with the state there (`docsIn`, from a mark where it opens: `docMark`): not after its own words (`cd a <<E`), and inside the $( ) it stands in.

Bash commands in the hook (src/bash-writes.mjs, since 0.26.5): the command is the first word after leading NAME=value words and wrappers (`unwrap`: sudo, env, nice, timeout, nohup, time, command, exec, ionice, stdbuf), a backslash-newline joins the lines where bash joins them (hereDocs, the risk on here-document bodies), `bash|sh -c '...'` strings, eval's string (in this shell, before follow makes its state not known) and here-documents fed to a shell are read as commands (recursively; a string known only when it runs is not known, with why, and a loop variable's strings are each read: `runString`), a script file run by source, `.` or a shell, run as the command (`./build.sh`, a #! file) or fed to a shell on stdin or by a pipe is not known (its text is not read; a path that is not there is quiet: `runFile`; until 2026-11-14 all of these were missed in silence), and `gitPaths` decides git checkout/restore: after `--` every word, `restore` its words, `checkout` without `--` only words that are files here (a branch or tag with a dot is not), `restore --staged` without --worktree nothing - src/bash-writes.mjs:153, src/bash-writes.mjs:172

src/pending.mjs reads the hosted upkeep branch (refs/remotes/*/readfirst/upkeep) from the clone's refs only, as of the last fetch (no-network-in-cli): `pending`, the MCP tool pending_map_edits and the PreToolUse hook (once per session per repository, after MIN_DAYS or MIN_MERGES) use it. The hook adds the line as context and never denies for it, even with --gate. The branch name is the hosted upkeep's: if the server renames it, this goes silent

hook state keys (src/cli.mjs): a file's absolute path (notes shown; checked at the stop), `touched:<path>` (no time left to look it up: checked at the stop, looked up on the next call), `start:<root>` (the session's first call in that repository that wrote nothing readfirst can name: the Stop hook then also checks every changed file whose mtime is newer, so a file a script wrote is not skipped), `pending:<root>` and `notrun:<root>:<state>` (the stop already blocked once for checks that did not run at this state of the files), and since 0.31.0 `call:<sig>` (every call the hook saw), `denied:<sig>` (the gate refused it) and `resent:<sig>:<time>` (the same call made again with no other in between), and in the release after 0.31.0 `find:<root>` (a Bash call ran readfirst find there), `findwords:<root>:<words>` (the words that find asked: a new name counts as searched for when one of them meets a word of the name), `nofind:<sig>:<names>` (the gate refused new code no find had asked about; a find run after it lets the same call through) and `nofindwrite:<sig>` (new code written without one; counted at the stop), and `shown:` and `read:` (the next risk), and `unknown:<hash>` (a Bash command that writes where shellWrites cannot tell: refused once with --gate, let through when made again; `commandKey` hashes the command with its folder and that folder's repository, and a key of the command alone, before 2026-11-14, still counts), `misread:<hash>` (a shell reader threw on it; also unknown) and `failed:<tool>:<error>` (the hook failed on a call and let it through; quoted values and numbers in the error are left out, so one kind of error is one key), `ask:`, `answer:`, `unsure:`, `untrue:`, `head:`, `base:` (the risk on src/answers.mjs), `unasked:`, `refused:`, `redone:` (own risks). runStopHook skips every tagged key but start and touched: a new kind of key must go into its tag list, or it is read as a file path (harmless only while stopFor drops paths git does not list).

the PreToolUse hook's notes say, for each rule and risk, its fixed id (`itemId` in src/cli.mjs: `rule:<id>`, or `risk:<group>:<8 hex of the SHA-1 of its text>`, so an edited risk text is a new item) and what the edit about to be made does to it (`brief` with ids): touched, not touched or not judged, from `judge` (src/trigger.mjs) on the change `textChange` computes from the file on disk and the edit applied to it (`editTexts`: Edit, MultiEdit with each edit in turn, replace_all, Write). `textChange` is a Myers line diff in linear space (middle snake; a copy of each round's furthest points ran a 5000-line Write out of heap and the hook died with no answer) written out as -U0 hunks for parsePatch, so the hook judges an edit as `diff` judges a commit. It has a budget (`DIFF_WORK` steps and the hook's deadline): past it the change is `unplaced`, and `noteStates` makes each item it did not find touched say not judged, too much to place. A file a Bash command writes has no edit to compare (not judged: no edit). A judge that throws makes every item say not judged: judging the edit failed, never no edit and never without notes. With --gate an item touched or not judged is asked until it has an answer (the risk on src/answers.mjs); one not touched is one line, not asked.

what the hook counts as read (src/cli.mjs, since 2026-11-13): `shown:<branch>:<path>` (the hook showed the file's notes on that branch) and `read:<branch>:<path>` (a Bash call ran `readfirst read` on the file there and its whole output came back: not to /dev/null, a file or a pipe, not cut by --limit; `bashReads` in src/bash-writes.mjs). Whether a file's notes are due, and whether --gate refuses, is read from these for the branch the repository is on now (`branchOf`; the commit when detached), never from the bare path alone: a mark left on another branch let an edit through without that branch's notes, and a CLI read was not counted at all, so a file read that way was refused the same. A `read:` mark counts from the next call on, and is kept only when its call is let through: the hook runs before the command, so in `readfirst read f; sed -i ... f` nobody has seen the notes when sed writes. A bare path with no `shown:` mark for it, from a state file an older readfirst wrote, still counts. A file let through by a `read:` mark that has no bare path yet is marked `touched:`, so the Stop hook still checks it. The reads are seen only in Bash calls the PreToolUse hook receives: a settings matcher without Bash sees none.

the PreToolUse hook gives every file a call writes its notes, each repository's lines once (a line for only some files names them) and every line, with nothing cut (0.27.1; before, the first 10 files and 12 lines a file, and files 11 and on were never checked at the stop). It has a budget (runHook's `budget`, 10 s of the 15 s Claude Code allows): files it had no time for are named in the notes, marked `touched:` for the Stop hook and looked up on the next call; with --gate the call is refused once, and made again at once (`resentNow`: the same call, nothing in between) it goes through with them named, however slow the lookup still is (until 2026-11-14 it was refused each time the lookup ran out of time again, with no end), and that retry is not counted as `resent:`. A file let through so and never looked up later (no bare path, `shown:` or `read:` mark) had its rules and risks asked nowhere: in a session the gate refused in (a `denied:` key), the stop names those not asked or answered, once per set (`unasked:<root>:<hash of the ids>`), and sends the agent to the notes, since an item never asked cannot be answered. Every refusal that says to make the same call again must let it through when made again as told, and a test in the tests group tries each. Speed comes from src/hook-cache.mjs, never from leaving files or lines out.

src/hook-cache.mjs keeps the import graph and brokeBefore results per repository in the hook's state folder between calls (mode 600; a file another user owns is ignored), keyed by HEAD, the file list, the changed config files and the readfirst version. Edges from changed JS/TS/Python/JSON files are read again from the files; any other changed file (Go, C#, Java: their edges depend on other files' text) rebuilds the whole graph. A new file importEdges reads to resolve imports (beside package.json, tsconfig/jsconfig) must go into `CONFIG` there, or edits to it are served stale. sentry (22,494 files): 3.1 s cold, 85 ms warm, the same edges as a full rebuild.

the Stop hook (`stopFor`) counts files the session committed (git log since its first mark) as edited, and since 0.27.1 also as changed when it checks the map's `requires` (change together): `committed` takes the mark's own second (git keeps whole seconds) so no committed file goes unchecked, `committedAfter` only later seconds so a commit from before the session never stands in for a partner the session left out. Before, a pair committed together in the session (package.json and server.json) was reported as left behind.

init --agent, setup and hook --install (installHook, addAgentLine, setupAgents) add to files people edit by hand, often with comments (JSONC). A file that does not parse as plain JSON is never rewritten and never stops the rest: init goes on and prints what to add by hand (hookSnippet, `SNIPPETS` in src/agents.mjs). Until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) init stopped at a .claude/settings.json with comments and wrote nothing after it. A new file that init or setup touches needs a test with a commented copy in the middle of the list. installHook also adds Bash to the matcher of a readfirst PreToolUse entry that does not cover it (an install from before the hook read Bash commands), and touches nothing else there, its command included: the old matcher is replaced in the file's own text when it is written there once, else the file is written out as JSON (test/install-matcher.test.mjs).

read and diff take a file path from the repository root, from the current folder or absolute (fromHere in main): until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) only the first worked, and `readfirst read ./x.mjs` in a subfolder said the file was not tracked. With --root (the MCP server, scripts) a relative path stays relative to the root. A new command that takes file arguments resolves them the same way; test from a subfolder and with an absolute path.

changedFiles picks what verify, diff and the Stop hook compare against: the --base given (an unknown one is an error that names it, not 'the clone is shallow': until 0.26.4 a typo in --base sent people to fetch more history), else origin/main, main, origin/master, master. On the base branch itself with no origin/<base> (changed.here) the base is HEAD: onBaseItself says only uncommitted changes are counted, and with none it fails asking for --base. Until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) verify said 'nothing to verify' there and passed with the committed changes unchecked. An empty set of changes must never read as a pass.

No hook may fail closed on its own trouble: a hook given arguments it does not know (an older readfirst under newer settings) answers with a systemMessage and exit 0 (letThrough in main; exit 2 refused every Edit and Bash call of a session until 0.26.4, readfirst#130), and hook --gate whose state cannot be saved (a full or read-only temp folder: addSeen throws) passes the notes as context instead of refusing (until 0.27.0, readfirst#133, every retry was refused again). Test with an unknown option and with an unwritable state folder.

bin/readfirst.mjs ends the process quietly when stdout or stderr is closed early (EPIPE: `readfirst read x | head -1`); until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) that crashed with a stack trace and exit 1. The handler rethrows every other error, and nothing in src may install a handler that swallows them. - bin/readfirst.mjs:5
src/action.mjs imports edgesWith, repoFiles, readMapFile and readText from cli.mjs, so changing how files are listed, import edges are built or the map is read also changes the GitHub Action

--timeout (seconds per check) is shared by verify (default 900) and `hook --stop` (default 600); the plain PreToolUse hook ignores it. main() passes it to runStopHook only when it is a number above 0 and reports anything else through letThrough (a systemMessage, exit 0), never as the default. The hook's own `timeout` in .claude/settings.json is a separate limit that must cover all the checks together, or Claude Code kills the Stop hook before the checks finish. A new option the Stop hook should honour has to be passed on in main(): until 0.29.1 --timeout was parsed and dropped.

`runStopHook` appends one JSON line per stop to readfirst-acted.jsonl in the temp folder (fields session, at, shown, asked, acted, notActed, resent, and, in the release after 0.31.0, noFind, the count of `nofindwrite:` marks, and since 2026-11-13 misread, the count of `misread:` marks, and failed, the list of `failed:` marks without the tag, and since 2026-11-14 unsure, the count of answers left unsure, untrue, the count the stop found not borne out, items, `itemTally` per item id, and unchecked, the count of repositories the stop could not check), and `hookReport` reads those lines back, keeping the last line of each session and treating a missing field as 0. Renaming or dropping a field makes lines written by an older readfirst count as zeros in `hook --report`, with no error. `asked` and `notActed` come only from a `stopFor` that reaches its result, so a stop that ends earlier adds nothing to them.

the gate asks for answers (src/answers.mjs, since 2026-11-14; until then a call refused with its notes went through when made again, read or not): `runHook` with --gate judges every Edit, Write, MultiEdit and Bash write, also of a file already shown (`notesFor` with gate: its notes are not shown again), and refuses while an item touched or not judged (`noteItems`) has no answer that holds (`answered`: the item touched by no names other than those it was asked by when answered, so a new name asks again; an item not judged is answered once a session). Notes with nothing to ask go through as context; a map that cannot be read says so in them. An answer is read only from `readfirst answer '<json>'` as the shell hands its argument over (`answerRuns`, through commandWords and its `raw` word: $( ), a variable even one the command sets, a here-document or a pipe is no answer), checked by `answersIn` (an id asked in this session, a kind, a because, a not-this whose symbols are among the names it was asked by, so none for an item not judged; with 4 or more items asked, an answer that would leave over half of them with an unsure last answer is refused, counted by item; every answer stays in the state) and kept as the reads are: only when its call is let through, from the next call on, so an answer and a write in one command is refused for the write. A bad answer is refused and nothing of it is kept. State: `ask:<JSON [item, by]>` and `answer:<JSON [item, kind, covered, symbols, because]>`. An unsure answer with no later one of another kind blocks the stop once (`openUnsure`, `unsure:<hash of the ids>`) and is counted as `unsure` in the stop's line. An item asked and never answered, on a file the session changed another way (the edit refused, the file written by a command), blocks the stop once naming it (an `unasked:` key, beside the budget risk's). The `readfirst answer` command only prints what it was given; it writes nothing.

the Stop hook checks the gate's answers against the change (`stopFor` in src/cli.mjs, since 2026-11-14), by each item's last answer (`lastAnswers` in src/answers.mjs) for the items of the files it checks: a not-this whose item the session's diff touches by a name outside its symbols (judged again by `judge`, from the session's start, `head:` and `base:` (the next risk), to the working tree now; a state with none, a start no longer under HEAD (a branch switch or a rebase), a start only partly known, or a diff git cannot give compares no not-this and says which; files a move of HEAD the session did not commit brought (the HEAD reflog since the start: all but `commit:`, amend, initial; a merge, pull, rebase, cherry-pick, squash) leave the diff and are named, else another's change refuses a right not-this; no reflog back to the start compares none; a start with no commit diffs from the empty tree git names, which differs in a SHA-256 repository), and a done whose item's checks (a rule's own, a risk's group's) did not all pass in this stop's run. A done on an item with no checks is not compared. The answers found are named and refuse the stop once for that set of items (`untrue:<root>:<hash of the ids>`), and every stop keeps them in its line: `untrue` (the count) and `items` (`itemTally`: per item id, asked, each kind of answer, not borne out). `hook --report` adds `items` up over the sessions, most asked first, every item named; `audit` reads the same lines (ACTED_LOG in the temp folder, read and never written) and names the rules and risks of its map that 3 sessions or more answered and more than half of them last answered not-this (`wideItems`, by the `last` answer each session's `items` keeps; a line without `last` counts any not-this; a session asked and giving no answer is not counted), as too wide. Until the start was kept, the branch's whole diff against main was judged, so a commit made before the session counted against a not-this.

`markHead` in runHook (src/cli.mjs) keeps where a session started in each repository, on its first call that wrote or could write there, before that call ran: `head:<sha>:<root>` (the commit, so the stop can tell the start is still under HEAD) and `base:<JSON [root, snapshot, untracked, count, why]>` (`baseOf`). The snapshot is `git stash create`: a commit of the tracked files as they were, which writes git objects nothing refers to (gc removes them) and no ref or stash entry (HEAD when nothing was changed; '' in a repository with no commit and nothing added; null when it failed, with `why`). stash create rewrites the index it reads even with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, so it runs on a copy of the index in the temp folder (GIT_INDEX_FILE); and the `git` helper sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for every call, so the hook's `git status` neither refreshes nor locks the user's index. A test checks the index's mtime after a first call. untracked lists the files git did not track then, which the stop does not count as the session's; past PRE_MAX (2,000) it is null and count says how many, and the stop compares no not-this there. readfirst keeps no copy of an untracked file, so one the session then changed, or added to git (the diff from the snapshot shows it as new from its first line), is left out of the diff and named at the stop as not compared. In a 7,102-file repository the copy, stash create and the untracked list add 40 to 66 ms to the first call. Until 2026-11-14 only the commit was kept, so changes uncommitted at the start and files untracked then counted as the session's.

a `stopFor` that throws (a broken .git/index makes its first `git status` fail, a git that is gone, a folder that is no longer a repository) no longer returns null: until 2026-11-14 that skipped every check the map lists and every answer comparison with no word, as if there were nothing to check. Its catch names the repository and the error, refuses the stop once per repository and kind of error (`unchecked:<root>:<hash>`, the error with quoted values and numbers left out, as for `failed:`; a state key the tag list in runStopHook skips) and says it again as a note on later stops. The session's line gains `unchecked`, the count of repositories not checked, and `hook --report` adds it up. A new early return in stopFor that means nothing could be checked must say so the same way. runStopHook does the same for a marked file whose repository git no longer finds (the hook marks only files inside one, so its .git or gitdir went away), naming the files with git's error; and changedFiles says a base branch whose ref file is there but names no readable commit is that, not 'no base branch'. git can be wrong with rc 0: the `git` helper throws when stderr has an error: or fatal: line (kept whole in `gitErrors`; errorText cuts neither them nor readfirst's own sentences, thrown with `ours`), and stopFor first checks the index against the hash at its end (git 2.43 reads a cut or flipped index without a word), and the one sharedindex.<hash> a split index names in its `link` extension (`sharedIndexOf` reads the entries to it; an index it cannot read is said, an old unused one is never checked) by its end and its name, and throws when a map in HEAD is missing from the working tree (a sparse checkout).

the find-first gate in `runHook` recognises `readfirst find` only by the `FIND_RUN` pattern (readfirst, readfirst@version, npx with --yes/-y, or a path ending in readfirst.mjs, followed by `find`) in a Bash call; any other way of running it (a shell alias, `node -e`, a script that wraps it) leaves no `find:<root>` mark and no `findwords:` mark, and the next edit that adds a function is refused as if find never ran. A find that did run opens the gate only for the new names it asked about (`findAsked`: a word of its query, read by `findQuery` with the options left out, meets a word of the name, by `words` and `meets` of src/find.mjs), or, for names the gate already refused once, any find run after that refusal: one search at the start no longer covers every function written afterwards. What counts as new code is `newCode`, which applies the edit to the file as it is on disk and compares the names `definitions` (src/find.mjs) finds in the whole file before and after (for Write, the new content against the file as it is; an edit whose old text is not in the file adds nothing); a change to `definitions`, `words` or `meets` changes what the gate refuses.

the gate (`runHook` with --gate) sees one tool call at a time, never the other calls of the response it came in: an agent sends several, they run one after another, and when the gate refuses one, those before it have run and those after it are judged on their own, so a definition refused while the edits that use it went in leaves a file half changed (2026-11-14, three sessions). Every refusal opens by naming the call it refuses (`callWhat`: the tool, the files, an Edit by the first line of its old text; and the hook input's `tool_use_id`) and says the others were not refused by it (`BATCH_LINE`); an error read against the wrong call of a response sent that call twice. Each refusal is kept as `refused:<sig>:<JSON [call, files]>`; a later call let through that writes one of those files, by any tool (a Bash command by the files its write reader names), marks it `redone:<sig>`, so the change made again as a MultiEdit, a Write or a `sed -i` counts. The Stop hook names every refused call with no later `redone:`, once for that set (`refused:said:<hash>`), when the session changed files. The hook input has `transcript_path` and `tool_use_id`, from which the other calls of the response could be read; readfirst does not read it, so any later write of the same file counts as the change made again, whatever it changed.

groups.title: the GitHub Action: one PR comment with the read list for the changed files, and a failed check when the map falls behind

checks.why: the Action against a fake GitHub API: post, update in place, broken map, read-only token, non-PR events, auto-fix commits

risks.text: composite actions do not set INPUT_* env vars, so action.yml maps each input to an env var by hand; a new input needs a line in action.yml and a read in src/action.mjs (`runAction`)
the existing PR comment is found by its first line (`MARKER`); changing `MARKER` makes every open PR get a second comment instead of an update
a 403 from a comment write is treated as a fork PR and swallowed by matching ': 403 ' in the message built by api(); changing that error text turns fork PRs into failed jobs

the script runs only when argv[1] ends with '/src/action.mjs', and action.yml calls it by that path; moving or renaming the file makes the Action exit successfully without doing anything - src/action.mjs:234
when the map has problems the comment shows the problems but no read list (`commentBody`, called from `runAction`), and the job fails unless fail-on-map-problems is 'false'

auto-fix writes to the PR branch through the contents API: only on a branch of this repository (never a fork), only when the branch's map equals the one this run read (else it would overwrite a newer push), and only what settleMap settles; anything a person must decide stays in the comment

the changed files still come from the GitHub API, but the 'Files in this PR that broke before' section reads the checkout's git log (brokeBefore) and says 'history not fetched (set fetch-depth: 200 on actions/checkout)' when the checkout is shallow; the workflow `init --ci` writes and this repository's ci.yml both set fetch-depth: 200, so keep the three in step

the Action's PR comment and `diff` render a judged read list with toMarkdown(..., { verdict }) (0.29.0): the verdict (src/verdict.mjs) first, then the rules and risks the change touches, then those it could not match (risks whose own files name a changed file open, group-wide ones folded), then the rest folded with their counts (not triggered, hot spots, flows, vocabulary, tests, users, broke before). The checks, change-together, being-replaced and other-repository rows are in the verdict and not listed again. toMarkdown returns before the plain layout when given a verdict, so a new section added to the plain layout is missing from diff and the PR comment unless verdictMarkdown shows it too (VERDICT_PLACES and its test catch a new list of the read list, not a new section of an old one). `read` and --json keep the plain layout. A risk is `named` only when it has `files`; a map whose risks carry no files gets every unmatched risk folded

action.yml runs `node` itself (composite): a self-hosted runner without Node gets a clear ::error:: from the `command -v node` guard instead of 'command not found'; the Action does not set up Node, because actions/setup-node would change the Node of the user's later steps - action.yml:35

a read list longer than one comment is split by splitComment (60,000 characters a part, cut only between top-level blocks; a <details> block is closed and reopened with '(continued)'); part N starts with partMarker(N), `<!-- readfirst:pr-comment:N -->`, and is found by it on the next push, as part 1 is by `MARKER`. Changing partMarker gives every open PR new parts; the job summary gets the whole body unsplit.

The Action finds its comment by the first line (`MARKER`; partMarker(N) for the parts of a long one) and edits it in place. Anyone can post a comment that starts with the marker: until 0.26.5 (readfirst#132, security) another user's such comment was taken as ours, the PATCH failed with 403, the 403 was read as a fork PR, and no readfirst comment was posted. Bots' marked comments are tried first, then the rest newest first, each PATCH that fails with 403 or 404 moves to the next, and a new comment is posted only when none can be edited. Test with a marked comment by another user.
when the map has problems the comment opens with a verdict whose Blocked line names them, then shows the problems but no read list, and the job fails unless fail-on-map-problems is 'false'

groups.title: the map format and checker, the first-draft map, import reading (JS/TS, Python and seven more languages) and the read list

checks.why: patterns, draft, check messages, imports and read list cases

risks.text: mapProblems rejects unknown fields, so a new map field must be added to the allowed-field list and made optional, and older readfirst versions will reject maps that use it; maps in users' repositories must keep passing under readfirst/map@1
the read list object (`readList`) is the --json output and what the Action renders; keep its field names and the readfirst/read-list@1 format string (`READ_LIST_FORMAT`)
patternToRegExp is used for group files, ignore, rule files and risk files alike; changing what a pattern matches moves files between groups in every user's map

test files are recognised by two separate regexes (isTest in readlist.mjs, which covers every language langs.mjs reads, and the top-level tests-folder check in draftMap); a new test naming convention goes into isTest, and into draftMap only if it is a top-level folder

imports are read with regexes: JS/TS and Python in src/imports.mjs (`importEdges`), Go, Rust, Elixir, C#, Java/Kotlin, Ruby and PHP in src/langs.mjs (`moreEdges`). Only edges that resolve to a tracked file count (workspace packages, tsconfig paths aliases and baseUrl, package.json #imports, and Python roots at each folder with manage.py, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg included), so packages from outside, aliases set up elsewhere (bundler config, tsconfig extends) and names the approximation misses (Rails constants used unqualified inside a module, C# types reached without a using) leave tests out of the read list

readlist.mjs and settleMap (map.mjs) read fixMap's change messages (`groups.<id>: added <pattern>`): readlist for the 'would add it to group' hint, settleMap to tell a new top-level folder from a file beside placed ones; rewording those messages silently breaks both

labels are personal: they live in .readfirst/local/, which keepLocal adds to .git/info/exclude; reading labels from anywhere else, or writing them into the map, would hand one person's notes to the whole team
the view page (`viewHtmlCity`) loads three.js 0.160.0 from cdn.jsdelivr.net (`THREE`) through an import map; without network it shows only the WebGL/connection notice

the view page (`viewHtmlCity`) only has interface strings for en and ko, and the language switch only toggles between them: a labels file for any other language (e.g. `prompt --labels ja`) is read and inlined but never shown, and the plain/technical switch appears only when the current language's file has "plain"

check, read, diff, verify and the Action settle a map that is only behind the code the way fix would (settleMap) and pass; only what fix cannot place, broken rules and new top-level folders fail. Making them strict again breaks every PR that adds a file

`audit`'s 'hot spots nothing checks' (`ownCheck` inside it) counts a group check as a check of its own only if fewer than half the groups share the same `run` string (always, if the map has under two groups). Adding one command such as `npm test` to most groups, or writing the same check with different text, changes which hot spots are listed. A rule check only counts when the rule's files cover the hot spot's file. - src/audit.mjs:173

readfirst's own files (the map, .readfirst/held.json and the exported .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc) belong to no group: isOwnFile in map.mjs (OWN_FILES and OWN_PATTERN) keeps them out of placement, and readlist.mjs reports them as status MAP. A new file readfirst writes into the checkout must be added there, or check fails with it as an unplaced file. The Cursor file name is matched twice (OWN_PATTERN in map.mjs and isCursorExport in export.mjs): change both together. The text export writes is compared byte for byte by `export --cursor --check`, so rewording it makes every user's CI fail until they re-export. - src/map.mjs:10

the agents setup knows are listed in several places: `AGENTS`, detectAgents, `PLAN` and `SNIPPETS` in src/agents.mjs, the notes-file list in addAgentLine (cli.mjs), the HELP text and the 'Wire every agent at once' section of docs/guide.md. A new agent must be added to all of them: without a `PLAN` entry setupAgents throws on it, and without a `SNIPPETS` entry the by-hand message for an unparsable file says only 'the readfirst MCP server'. Setup writes a file only when it parses as plain JSON (or, for Codex, when no [mcp_servers.readfirst] table exists), and a readfirst key that is already there is never compared or updated.

the scar rules in src/history.mjs (`SIGNALS`, `NOISE`, NOT_CODE, `TEST`, scar, spreadScars) are a copy of the hosted version's lib/history.mjs, kept in one module so the hosted side can import them from the package; a change to the regexes or weights changes what `read`, `diff`, the Action and `audit` call a scar, and the threshold constants (MIN_WEIGHT 2 for a file, BROKE_MOST_MIN_SCORE 2 with BROKE_MOST_MIN_COMMITS 2 for audit) decide when a young repository shows nothing; NOT_TRAP only trims the audit ranking

flows have no count limit since 0.25.0 (OLD_MAX_FLOWS 500 before): the map stores every path, and a reader caps only its own work. A map with more than 500 flows fails a CLI before 0.25.0, so pins.mjs FIELD_SINCE warns in `check` when the pinned readfirst is older, and the server must not write more than 500 for such a pin

a target that is not tracked (deleted in the change, or new and not added) keeps status NOT_TRACKED and its 'not a tracked file' note, but readList still gives it its group's checks, risks and deprecation, and the rules, requires and dependents entries that match its path: verify, diff and the Action (which passes removed files too) rely on this so a change made only of deletions still runs its group's checks. It gets no tests or unseen entries; since 0.27.0 its users are listed, from import edges built over the tracked files plus the targets (edgesWith), with a 'still imported by' note, and a target that settling left in no group is looked up in the map as written (`before`). - src/readlist.mjs:102

readList lists every test and direct user unless a limit is passed (`read --limit`, the Action's `limit` input), and `truncated` says how many a limit cut. No caller passes a limit of its own any more (the hook passed 10, view 5 and the Action 30 before 0.27.1, and view counted the five as all the users): a new caller that cuts a list must say what it cut.

the hooks keep importEdges' result between calls (src/hook-cache.mjs): edges from a changed JS/TS/Python/JSON file are read again from that file alone, with the config files in its `CONFIG` (package.json, tsconfig/jsconfig, pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg). A resolver that starts reading another file, or edges of those languages that come to depend on other files' text, must be added there, or the hook serves stale edges until the next commit.

bashWrites (src/bash-writes.mjs) is a hand-written shell reader, and every syntax it misses is a write the PreToolUse hook gives no notes for and, unless the file changed after the session's first mark, the Stop hook does not check; every syntax it misreads as a write puts notes on a command that only reads. Both have happened: &> and &>> (0.26.4); quotes not opening again inside $( ), so i>=0 in python -c became a write to =0 (0.26.4); NAME=val, sudo/env/nice/timeout wrappers, backslash-newline and bash -c strings (0.26.5, readfirst#132); a branch or tag with a dot and restore --staged read as writes (0.26.5); 2> and >|, (cd d && ...), pushd, globs and ~ missed, and (( x > 0 )), # comments, patch -p 1, remote or dry-run rsync read as writes (0.27.0, readfirst#133); a cd inside ( ) carried on past its ), so the hook showed another repository's notes, the ) stuck to the last word (`f.txt)`) and a redirect after the ) went into the subshell's folder (0.27.4: parens() in bash-writes.mjs; a { } group keeps its cd, as the shell does). a $( ) or backtick argument was split into words, so `sed -i ... $(grep -rl x src docs)` named src and `docs)` as written (0.30.0: words() keeps it one word, and add() leaves it out). Variables had no value and backslashes were kept: after `S=/a; cd $S` nothing relative was named, `> $F` was dropped, `a\&b.js` named a\&b.js, and `do sed -i ... f` in a loop was not read (2026-11-13: shellWord, follow, KEYWORDS in opening). The > of $(( )) and $[ ] was read as a redirect, so `echo $((1 > 0))` named a file 0 (2026-11-13: arithEnd, read by blank, closeOf, shellWord and opening). A redirect glued to a word (`echo hi>f`, `x=1>f`) was missed, `a\>b` was a write (2026-11-13: `OPERATOR`, one list for words, redirects, withoutRedirects). Still missed (2026-11-09): a write inside an awk program (print ... > file). A new case needs a test of the written form and one of the look-alike that only reads.

The bracket table (src/bash-writes.mjs, 2026-11-14): `scanText` reads quotes, $( ), backticks, (( )), $(( )), $[ ], ( ) and <( ) / >( ) in one pass with a stack, and blank, closeOf, arithEnd, words and lift all ask it (`table`, kept for the last 256 texts and dropped with BODIES). An index the table holds no opener at is -1: nothing scans again from there (a reader asking past a ' that never closes took time by the square). Whether a (( is arithmetic is decided where it opens, from where each ( closes (`pairs`): read as arithmetic until its ) and taken back, its first ( ) lost its <( ) and (( )). Before, each found brackets its own way: a regex one ( deep, a closeOf calling itself per level (out of stack at 4,000), scans again from each opener (quadratic). `lift` takes each $( ), backtick, <( ) and >( ) out of the command (placeholders `$(@N)`, a backtick pair, `/dev/fd/@N`, @ a private-use character the command does not hold (`freeMark`; none free: not read); BODIES holds the bodies while shellWrites or bashReads runs), so the command is split and its words read with nothing inside a substitution to mislead them (it was split at a ; or | inside one: `(echo $(cd /a; pwd) > f)` lost its write), and shellWrites reads each body after the command as a subshell, from a copy of the state where it stood, one after another from a list, never by a call per level (8,000 deep does not run out of stack). Unknown parts are put back (`unlift`) only in what shellWrites returns: put back for each word, each level held all the levels below it; a <( ) whole, not `/dev/fd/` and its body. A quote, ( or (( that never closes is a plain character, as before; a $( ), backtick or <( ) that never closes is hidden, as bash cannot parse it. Known gaps: a case pattern's ) inside a $( ) closes it; code bash cannot parse inside a closed $( ) is still read; backticks do not nest. test/bash-bracket-table.test.mjs pins the shapes against bash and the time as linear (slope under 1.5).

Every file readfirst writes in a user's checkout goes through a check that the real path stays inside the repository: mustBeInside (src/cli.mjs: init, fix, export --cursor, verify --record, view), outsideRepo (src/agents.mjs: setup, hook --install) or, for setup --git, the `ok` check in src/git-hooks.mjs, which resolves the real path of the hooks folder and of each hook file and allows only the repository and its git folder. A CLAUDE.md, .claude, .cursor or .github that is a symlink to a place outside would otherwise be written through, into the user's home or another project (setup until 0.26.4, readfirst#130; export, init, fix and view until 0.26.5, readfirst#132, security). A new write, or a new file setup or export touches, needs the same check and a test with a symlinked folder and a symlinked file.

JSON a user wrote (the map, package.json, tsconfig, .claude/settings.json, the event file) may start with a UTF-8 byte order mark that npm and editors accept and JSON.parse does not: until 0.26.4 (readfirst#130) such a map failed as 'not valid JSON'. Read user files through readText (src/cli.mjs) or unBom (src/map.mjs); a JSON.parse straight on readFileSync of a user file is the bug. A new file read needs a test with a BOM.

find (src/find.mjs) lists definitions (`definitions`): for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and the <script> of .vue and .svelte files they are the declarations the one reader finds (src/code.mjs), filtered by find's own choices in `readDefinitions`: no plain values (a constant holding a list or table of names is found apart from them, by `listsOf`, from the same declarations and lexed lines: its name and the strings with no space, object keys and alternatives of a pattern (`a|b`) written in it, never its comment (the comment above a list matched lists of other things for most queries); `definitions` gives them only with `{ lists: true }`, which only find passes, so the find gate and the trigger engine do not see them), no names under three letters, no private #names, no noise words; what a CommonJS module puts on `exports` and a function in the object a module exports as a whole are listed, a property of any other object is not (an options object passed to a call would flood the list). The comment of a definition is the reader's `top` plus a Python docstring, and the comment a file opens with (`headerOf`) is matched for the file as a whole, once, never for each definition in it (that listed every function of a module whose header gave an example). For Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, Java, Kotlin and C# it still knows definitions only through its line regexes (`DEFS`): a declaration shape none of them matches is absent from `readfirst find`, and an agent writes the function again; a new language or syntax goes into `DEFS` with a test of the declaration and of a line that only looks like one (a call, a string, a comment). The find gate and the trigger engine's bounds for those languages read the same list, so a change here changes both.

draftChecks and workspaceChecks (src/map.mjs) write commands into the user's map, and verify and the Stop hook later run them in a shell with the user's rights. A drafted check must only read (no lint --fix, prettier --write, jest -u or --updateSnapshot: `REWRITES`), end by itself (no watch script: vitest without run, jest --watch, a dev server: `WATCHES`; verify hung until 0.26.4), use the project's runner (poetry run pytest, uv run pytest; a Makefile test := is a variable, not a target), and quote every package name, folder or script name read from the repository (pnpm --filter 'a; touch x' ran touch x until 0.26.5, readfirst#132, security). codexConfig (src/agents.mjs) must not write a second [mcp_servers.readfirst] table (0.27.0). A new drafted check needs a test with a hostile name and with a script that writes or watches.

A group risk with `files` shows for those files in any group (risksNaming in src/map.mjs, used by readList, audit, view and export --cursor; 0.27.2). Before, only the file's own group was read, so a risk naming a file of another group showed for no file and check passed. unshownRisks lists risks whose text names a tracked file that does not show them: `about` (named in the first clause, before the first : ; , or '. ') is listed first and fails check --strict; a later mention is listed after and never fails. A new reader of group risks must go through risksNaming, or cross-group risks go unseen there again.

setup --git (src/git-hooks.mjs, `setupGitHooks`) writes the hooks git runs: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (.git/hooks, core.hooksPath, the main repository's .git/hooks for a worktree), and for husky (core.hooksPath .husky/_ or .husky) the user's .husky/<hook>, never husky's own _ folder. It adds one line and never replaces a hook; a hooks folder outside the repository and its git folder (a global core.hooksPath shared by every repository), a hook file that is a link out of them, a hook that hands over with exec (the pre-commit framework's: a line after it never runs) and one that is not a shell script are printed for adding by hand. The hooks call `npx --yes readfirst check` and `verify`, so they need the map (setup --git refuses without one) and npx at commit time; check reads the working tree, so an untracked file that is not ignored blocks a commit until the map places it. A new hook or a new hook manager needs a test of where it writes and of what it leaves alone (test/setup-git.test.mjs).

src/trigger.mjs judges each risk and rule of a change's read list (`judge`, used by `diff`, the Action and the PreToolUse hook's notes, not by `read`; declaration bounds from `declarations`, which asks the one reader in src/code.mjs): what it is about is the backticked names and the code-looking names (camelCase, snake_case, UPPER_CASE with _) declared in the files it is shown for, the files its text names or the changed files (for a group's risk, only changed files of its own group: a vendored copy's NOT_CODE touched a risk about the package's until 0.31.0), plus its path:line evidence, which is carried from the file before the change to where it is now (toNew, from the hunk headers). Triggered when a changed line falls in that declaration (bounds from the file's structure; in a language src/code.mjs does not read, `approximateBounds`, up to the next declaration indented no deeper, the wide reading on purpose) or the name is in an added or removed line of code, read in its place in the file by `changedCode` (not in docs, the map, config, comments, strings or template text: on its own PR the map edit and trigger.mjs's comments named runHook and changedFiles); a plain lowercase word counts only as a function in the item's own files and never by appearing in the diff (a test's own `run` helper and the word `files` made risks read as touched on readfirst#139). An item naming nothing found is triggered by its files, as before, and a not-triggered one is listed with its reason, never dropped. Evidence that has drifted from its code (line 266 of src/cli.mjs pointed into verifyChecks for a risk about rootOf until 0.28.0) gives a wrong verdict: since 0.30.0 a line outside everything its item names is marked as such in the verdict, `check` lists it (evidenceDrift; --strict fails) and `fix` moves it only where git shows the code moving (moveEvidence). Write an example line number in prose, not as path:line, or it is read as evidence.

What evidence `path:line` is about in `judge` and `evidenceDrift` (src/trigger.mjs): the declaration the line belongs to (`scopeOf` in src/code.mjs: the function around a one-line local, the declaration below a doc comment or a decorator), or one entry of a table when the text names the entry's key (`entryNamed`, `entryAt`: the first string of an object in an array, or a property's name), so a risk about one pattern of a long table is not touched by a change to another. Only a line no declaration holds is judged by the ten lines around it. Evidence inside a table entry whose key the text does not name is about the whole table, and `check` lists it as having no anchor: name the key in the text. A file the reader cannot finish (it ends inside a template, a string or a comment: `unfinished`) counts as wholly touched and `unseenIn` (src/readlist.mjs) lists it.

src/verdict.mjs writes the verdict from the read list by template, in en or ko (VERDICT_TEXT): every count it gives must be of rows shown below it, and every line a reader must act on (blocked, to do) must come from a row, never from a guess. A new kind of row the verdict should count goes into sortRows or verdictLines and into every language of VERDICT_TEXT: a string in `en` alone would throw for `ko` at render time (t.x is not a function), and test/verdict.test.mjs fails on a language missing a key. The language is `diff --lang`, else the one verdict language among this clone's labels (diffLang in src/cli.mjs), else en; the Action reads the `language` input. An unknown code is said in the verdict and the job log, never silently English. Only the template is translated: the map's text is never machine-translated here (no-network-in-cli, no model)

`subjectPaths` (src/trigger.mjs): a path in a risk's first clause, with or without an extension, is what the risk is about: a change to it triggers the risk unless the risk already names code in that file (`judge`), and readfirst's own files never count; `unmatchedItems` counts such a risk as judgeable. A file named only after the first clause judges nothing by itself (vendor/readfirst/VERSION read as not triggered until 0.32.0)

`filesWithoutNames` (src/trigger.mjs): a risk whose `files` are all exact paths (no `*` or `?`) with nothing declared in them (a workflow, a Dockerfile, a JSON or YAML file) is about those files: a change to one triggers it in `judge`, and `unmatchedItems` counts it as judgeable. One pattern among the files, or one file with a declaration, and it is judged by its names as before. `judge` gets the files from the read list row (`files` on a risk row, set in readList of src/readlist.mjs for a group risk and for one found by risksNaming): a row built without it is judged as if the risk had no files. Rules are not judged this way.

src/code.mjs is the one reader of code (`lex`, `tokens`, `closeOf`, `declarations`, `scopeOf`, `scriptBlocks`): one pass over the characters with the state carried from line to line, then one walk over the tokens with the brackets that are open. Nothing in it matches a pattern against a single line. A shape it misreads becomes a snippet in test/code.test.mjs with a parser's answer first, and is then fixed in the walk or in its lists of tokens (`NEEDS_MORE`, `CONTINUES`, `TYPE_BEFORE`, `OBJECT_BEFORE`, `STATEMENT_HEADS`), never by a rule for that one line: rules per line are what it replaces. One misread now travels down the file (a string or bracket left open shifts everything after it), where a reader per line kept it on its line. Its known guesses are the todo tests in test/code.test.mjs (JSX text on a line of its own outside parentheses, `await` at a line's end, a method named `catch` or `with` in an object, a callee that begins with a parenthesis). The trigger engine (src/trigger.mjs), `unseenIn` (src/readlist.mjs), `unusedCode` (src/audit.mjs), find's `definitions` and the find gate (`newCode` in src/cli.mjs) read through it; the shape patterns (src/shapes.mjs) read through it too. src/langs.mjs still blanks comments by regex (`noComments`, `blank`) for the languages the reader has no mode for. A second reader of strings, comments or brackets written beside it is how five of them came to exist.

src/shapes.mjs holds the published shapes (`PATTERNS`: queryset, str-method, str-replace, js-string, js-replace, js-expect-promise) and the machinery that looks for any list of shapes (`candidates(file, patterns)`, `discardedResults(files, fileText, { patterns })`); the hosted version passes its own list, so do not add the server's other shapes here, they stay hosted. What is code on a line comes from the one reader (`lex` in src/code.mjs, once per hunk: a hunk starts where the patch does), and the function around a call from its tokens and `declarations` (`enclosingFunction`: a declared function, or a brace after `=>` or after a `)` that does not follow if, for, while, switch, catch or with); no helper here skips a string or a comment itself, and one that does is the copy this file had four of. A pattern's own `find` is called as `find(stmt, code)`: the statement's text and the same characters as the lexer left them; it must close or count its call on the code with `closeOf` (exported, for lists given from outside too), never on the text, or it stops at a parenthesis inside a string and misses the finding (js-expect-promise did for `expect(load(')')).resolves`, 0.32.0). js-expect-promise leaves out files on vitest or bun test (notIn: a *.vitest.* name or an import of vitest or bun:test), which fail such a test themselves

`unseenIn` (src/readlist.mjs) now gives two kinds of entry: a module loaded by a computed name has `line`, and a file the reader cannot finish (`unfinished` in src/code.mjs) has none. A caller that prints `path:line` or counts computed loads must keep only the entries with `line`, as `audit` does (`computed` is the entries with a line, `unfinished` the rest), or it prints `path:undefined`.

`spansOf` (src/trigger.mjs) reads a name from an item's text only when it is in backticks or has a shape only code has (camelCase, snake_case, UPPER_CASE with an underscore, a call such as `main()`). A bare capital word with no underscore (CLI, API, URL, JSON, VERSION, FLAGS) is prose: 0.30.0 counted them, and a risk about "the CLI version" read as touched by a change to a line using a constant called CLI. A risk about a constant FLAGS must write `FLAGS`. A risk written before that rule and now judged by nothing is listed by `unmatchedItems` with `backtick`, the bare capital words its files declare, so `audit` can say what to put in backticks.

risks.text: test/bash-fuzz.test.mjs runs 3,000 random scripts (seed 187, the reviewer's generator copied unchanged) through bash, each in an empty folder under a temporary root with an empty environment and a 5 s limit, and pins the commands whose writes shellWrites misses or names falsely in test/bash-fuzz-baseline.json. A change to src/bash-writes.mjs that fixes one fails it with the line to take out of the baseline; one that adds one fails with the command. Never add a command to the baseline to make it pass. It takes about 13 s of npm test's time, and is skipped, with the reason, where bash cannot be found.

npm test only runs test/*.test.mjs, so a test in a subfolder or with another file name never runs. It loads test/setup.mjs first (`node --import ./test/setup.mjs --test`), which turns commit signing off for the tests' git processes and gives each test process a temp folder of its own, removed when it ends. A test file run by hand without `--import ./test/setup.mjs` gets neither: on a machine set to sign every commit its commits ask the signing service (a hosted agent session's service ran out of file handles after a day of test runs, and then no commit could be made, 2026-11-11), and its temp folders stay. rules.rule: the readfirst command reads only the checkout: no network calls, no model calls, no API key (src/pending.mjs reads the clone's refs as of the last fetch, never fetches)
rules.why: it runs in agents' sandboxes and on private code; only the Action talks to the GitHub API

rules.rule: no runtime dependencies: Node's standard library only
rules.why: npx readfirst must start fast and nothing third-party runs on users' code

rules.rule: every tracked file is in exactly one group or in ignore, except readfirst's own files (the map, .readfirst/held.json and the exported .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc, see isOwnFile), and every group and rule pattern matches a tracked file; check fails otherwise
rules.why: this is what stops the map from quietly falling behind the code; the exported Cursor files must not need a group, or committing them would fail check --strict

rules.rule: maps written for readfirst/map@1 (`MAP_FORMAT`) keep passing (`mapProblems`): never rename or remove a map field or make an optional one required without a new format version
rules.why: map.json files live in users' repositories and CI fails on any map problem

rules.rule: the read list JSON (`readList`) keeps its field names under readfirst/read-list@1 (`READ_LIST_FORMAT`)
rules.why: agents and tools read `readfirst read --json` and `diff --json`

rules.rule: only `readfirst init`, `readfirst setup`, `readfirst fix`, `readfirst hook --install` and `readfirst view` write files in the checkout: init writes the map (never over an existing one without --force) and, with --agent, does what setup does, and with --ci .github/workflows/readfirst.yml (never over an existing one); setup --git adds one line to the pre-commit and pre-push hooks inside the repository or its git folder (src/git-hooks.mjs); setup adds the read-first line to agent notes files and readfirst's entry to the project's own agent configs (.claude/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .gemini/settings.json, .codex/config.toml, opencode.json), keeping what is there and never rewriting a file it cannot parse, and never writes outside the checkout (the user's home folder is printed, not written); fix writes only the map; hook --install writes only .claude/settings.json and keeps what is already there; view writes only under .readfirst/local/ (the page) and adds one line to this clone's .git/info/exclude, never anything git tracks; the plain `hook` writes only its state file and its cache (src/hook-cache.mjs) in the temp folder; `hook --stop` writes only a line in that state file (the checks it said did not run) and one line per stop in readfirst-acted.jsonl in the temp folder (step 4: asked, done, not done) and runs only the base branch's check commands, like verify; check, prompt (with or without --labels), read, diff, find, answer, audit, scan, pending and the mcp server never change the checkout; export --cursor writes and removes only .cursor/rules/readfirst-*.mdc; verify writes nothing itself except, with --record, .readfirst/held.json (which rules held, at which commit), and only runs the commands the map lists, which may write as they would when run by hand; the Action writes nothing in the checkout, and with auto-fix only commits the map that fix would write to the PR branch through the API
rules.why: agents run read and diff freely before every change, and the hook runs before every edit, so it must not touch the working tree

rules.rule: the Action keeps one comment per PR (`MARKER`, `partMarker`, `splitComment`), plus one more for each 60,000 characters a long read list needs, and edits them in place on each push; a part a longer list left behind is emptied with a line saying so, never deleted, and nothing in the comment is cut
rules.why: a new comment on every push floods the PR, and a comment cut short hides what the map says (it was cut at 60,000 characters until 0.27.1)

rules.rule: a read-only token (PR from a fork) must not fail the Action (`runAction`): the read list goes to the job summary instead
rules.why: contributors from forks would otherwise get a red check they cannot fix

rules.rule: the Action takes the PR's changed files from the GitHub API (`pages` in `runAction`), not from git history
rules.why: actions/checkout defaults to a shallow clone, so any checkout depth must work

rules.rule: the public code holds no hosted-version logic: the prompts and steps that fill the map stay on the server
rules.why: the free code is MIT and public; the paid value is the server's judgement.

rules.rule: nothing readfirst finds is cut to look shorter: a list cut to a fixed size for output (slice(0, N), a slice from the end such as slice(-30), a count that stops a loop) names the rest or says where it is, in a `cut:` comment on that line or the one above
rules.why: the owner's rule (2026-11-09): no bug hidden, no check skipped; fourteen silent cuts were found in two days, each hiding files, tests, lines or findings; verify's last-30-lines cut said nothing of the earlier lines until 0.27.4
